senate_races.long_description: Scott Colom, a Democratic prosecutor, has mounted an unexpectedly competitive challenge to Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, a first-term Republican who has been reliably aligned with President Trump. While Ms. Hyde-Smith is still favored in conservative Mississippi, Mr. Colom would be the first Black senator elected from the state since Reconstruction.

Senator Dan S. Sullivan, a Republican, is trying to hold on to his seat against former Representative Mary Peltola, a Democrat. The wild card in the four-person ranked-choice race is the presence of Daniel J. Sullivan, a retiree in a small fishing village who has the same name as the incumbent.

Senator Bill Cassidy lost his Republican primary this year after President Trump targeted him for voting to convict him in his second impeachment trial. Now the seat Mr. Cassidy held for over a decade is up for grabs, and Representative Julia Letlow, who is backed by Mr. Trump, is heavily favored to win it over Jamie Davis, a Democratic farmer.

Senator Ashley Moody, the Republican incumbent, is on the Senate ballot for the first time, having been appointed last year to finish Marco Rubio’s term. She faces State Representative Angie Nixon, a progressive who won the Democratic primary in an upset.

Representative Ashley Hinson, a Republican, is vying to maintain party control of the seat held by retiring Senator Joni Ernst. Polls have shown her locked in a tight race against Josh Turek, a Democratic state representative, in a state that President Trump won three times.

Senator Darline Graham, the Republican appointed to fill her deceased brother Lindsey Graham’s seat, is running for a full term of her own. Dr. Annie Andrews, a Democrat and a pediatrician, is hoping Ms. Graham’s inexperience and her ties to President Trump can help her flip a seat in a state that hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1998.

In one of the most expensive and consequential Senate races of this cycle, Senator Jon Husted, a Republican, is facing a challenge from Sherrod Brown, a Democrat. Mr. Brown lost his seat in 2024 after three terms in the Senate.

Senator Roger Marshall, a first-term Republican, is trying to survive an unexpectedly competitive race in deep-red Kansas. He faces Adam Hamilton, a centrist Democrat who has sought to corral farmers’ anger at economic conditions under President Trump.

Dan Osborn, a mechanic, former union leader and military veteran running as an independent, is challenging Senator Pete Ricketts, a Republican scion of an influential billionaire family with deep ties to Nebraska. To clear the way for Mr. Osborn’s bid, the Democratic primary winner, Cindy Burbank, declined the party’s nomination, potentially consolidating the anti-incumbent vote in the conservative stronghold.

Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic former public health official, is in a competitive race against former Representative Mike Rogers, a Republican who narrowly lost his Senate bid in 2024. The contest has become a key test for progressives, who are backing El-Sayed.
Senator Susan Collins, a Republican, is seeking a sixth term against the Democrat Troy Jackson in the toughest political environment she has faced over her 30-year career.

Representative Barry Moore, a third-term Republican and longtime Trump loyalist, is running for the Senate seat being vacated by Tommy Tuberville, who is running for governor. Mr. Moore’s Democratic opponent, Everett Wess, a former judge and lawyer, is a long shot in deep-red Alabama.

A late withdrawal by the incumbent Republican, Steve Daines, left a Senate seat open in a historically conservative state. Kurt Alme, a Republican backed by President Trump, faces an unusually fractured field after national Democrats and state leaders shifted support toward an independent candidate, Seth Bodnar, instead of the Democrat who won the party’s primary, Alani Bankhead.

The race to replace the retiring Senator Tina Smith, a Democrat, pits the state’s lieutenant governor, Peggy Flanagan, a Democrat, against Michele Tafoya, a sports journalist and a first-time candidate. The two have sparred over fraud in statewide programs and rising costs attributed to the Iran war and the Trump administration’s tariff policies.
Senator Tom Cotton, a Trump ally and the third-ranking Republican in the chamber, is heavily favored to win a third term. He is facing Hallie Shoffner, a Democrat and sixth-generation farmer.

Representative Andy Barr, a Republican, is running to succeed the retiring Senator Mitch McConnell, whose poor health came under scrutiny in recent months. Mr. Barr faces Charles Booker, a progressive former state lawmaker who has run for the Senate twice before.

Senator Bill Hagerty, a Trump-backed Republican, is seeking a second term in a state that President Trump won by nearly 30 points in 2024. His opponent, the Democratic environmental justice activist Marquita Bradshaw, previously ran for Senate in 2020 and 2024.

James Talarico, a state legislator, is trying to become the first Democrat in more than three decades to win a statewide election in Texas. He is facing Ken Paxton, the Republican state attorney general, in a race that is one of the most expensive American campaigns ever.

Nearly 20 years ago, John E. Sununu, a Republican, lost his Senate seat to Jeanne Shaheen, a Democrat. Now she is retiring, and Mr. Sununu is trying to make a comeback. He is facing Representative Chris Pappas, a low-key Democrat in his fourth term.
Senator Jeff Merkley is running for re-election in a solidly Democratic state. Among his challengers are State Senator David Brock Smith, a Republican, and Gary Lyndon Dye, a Libertarian.

Senator Jon Ossoff, a Democrat, is seeking a second term in Georgia, a battleground that both parties this cycle initially considered the toughest for Democrats to hold onto. He is facing Representative Mike Collins, a Republican who won President Trump’s endorsement in the primary.

Markwayne Mullin left the Senate to become secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, and his replacement, Alan Armstrong, is ineligible to seek a full term under state law. Representative Kevin Hern, a Trump ally, is the clear favorite to win the open seat.

Roy Cooper, the Democratic former North Carolina governor, and Michael Whatley, the former Republican National Committee chairman, are competing to succeed Senator Thom Tillis, a Republican who is retiring.
Senator Shelley Moore Capito is running for a third term in West Virginia, a Republican stronghold. She faces Rachel Fetty Anderson, a lawyer and a Democratic former city councilwoman in Morgantown.

Senator Mike Rounds, a Republican, is running for a third term in one of the country’s most conservative states. Public polling has been limited, but some surveys have shown him in a closer-than-usual race with Brian Bengs, an independent. The Democratic nominee withdrew from the ballot.
Senator Mark Warner, a Democrat, is seeking a fourth term in a state that is considered solidly blue. He faces Bert Mizusawa, a retired general who easily won the Republican primary.

Senator Jim Risch, 83, a Republican, is heavily favored to win a fourth term in Idaho, a state President Trump carried by more than 36 percentage points in 2024. His toughest challenge comes from Todd Achilles, one of several independents challenging Republicans across the country this year.

Illinois’ open Senate seat, now held by retiring Senator Dick Durbin, a Democrat, is likely to remain blue. Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton, a progressive, is favored to prevail over her Republican opponent, Don Tracy, a former chairman of the state Republican Party.

Senator John Hickenlooper, a moderate incumbent, is running for a second term in a solidly Democratic seat. He faces Mark Baisley, a Republican state senator, and Bob Chew, a Navy veteran and former Republican who is running as an independent.

Senator Ben Ray Luján, a Democrat, is running for a second term in a solidly blue state against Larry E. Marker, a former oil and gas producer who won the Republican nomination as a write-in candidate.

Senator Chris Coons, a Democrat, is heavily favored to win re-election in a state that Kamala Harris carried by about 15 percentage points two years ago. His Republican challenger is Mike Katz, a doctor who has served in Delaware’s State Senate.
Senator Cory Booker, a Democrat and former Newark mayor elected to the Senate in 2013, faces Justin Murphy, a Republican attorney.

In deep-red Wyoming, the state’s lone at-large House member, Harriet Hageman, is favored to succeed Senator Cynthia Lummis, a Republican, who is retiring after serving one term. Ms. Hageman faces James Byrd, a Democratic former state lawmaker.

Senator Ed Markey, 80, a Democrat whose progressive bona fides helped him turn back a much younger challenger in the primary, is running for re-election in a solidly Democratic state. He faces John Deaton, a Republican lawyer and a Marine veteran.

Senator Jack Reed, a Democrat, is seeking a sixth term in a state that has not sent a Republican to the Senate since 2000. He is being challenged by Raymond McKay, a Republican activist who was formerly the network and telecommunications manager for the city of Warwick, R.I.

governor_races.long_description: Republicans see Kansas as an opportunity to flip the governorship on an otherwise foreboding electoral map. Ty Masterson, the Republican nominee and president of the Kansas Senate, has aligned himself with President Trump. State Senator Cindy Holscher, who emerged from a fractious Democratic primary, is trying to hold the seat for her party.

Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, a former state lawmaker, is trying to become Alaska’s youngest governor ever and its first Democratic one since 1998. Under Alaska’s top-four ranked-choice voting system, he faces three Republicans: Bernadette Wilson, owner of a garbage collection company; Treg Taylor, a former attorney general; and Dave Bronson, a former Anchorage mayor. Ms. Wilson has President Trump’s endorsement.

Byron Donalds, the Republican backed by President Trump, is vying to continue the party’s dominance in the governor’s mansion. A victory would make him Florida’s first Black governor. He faces David Jolly, a former Republican congressman who became a Democrat last year. No Democrat has held the governorship in Florida since the late 1990s.

Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Trump ally, is the front-runner to become Tennessee’s first female governor. She faces a number of challengers, including Jerri Green, a Democratic Memphis councilwoman. There are also two surprisingly robust independent challenges from Lauren Pinkston, an academic, and David Hatley, a businessman.

Gov. Kelly Ayotte, a Republican who served in the U.S. Senate, is seeking re-election, while her challenger, Cinde Warmington, a Democratic lawyer and former lobbyist, argues that Ms. Ayotte would enable “more Trump chaos” in a second term.

Senator Tommy Tuberville, the Republican firebrand and former Auburn football coach, is facing Doug Jones, the Democrat he ousted in 2020. Mr. Tuberville’s campaign has been defined by his alliance with President Trump and a steady drumbeat of anti-Muslim and anti-immigrant messaging, while Mr. Jones leaned on his Senate record and civil rights work.

Mike Mazzei, a former state senator, emerged from a competitive Republican primary with President Trump’s endorsement and is favored to hold the open seat for his party. But Democrats, whose candidates are usually trounced in statewide races, have invested in the race and expressed hope that their nominee, State Representative Cyndi Munson, could be competitive.

In a rematch of 2022, Democratic incumbent Tina Kotek faces Christine Drazan, a conservative Republican state legislator. Ms. Kotek’s low approval rating and the state’s slow recovery from the pandemic have made this a closer campaign than the state’s demographics would suggest.
Gov. Phil Scott, a moderate Republican seeking a sixth term, is facing Amanda Janoo, a progressive Democrat and a political newcomer whose campaign has picked up unexpected momentum.

Greg Abbott, the well-moneyed, longtime governor of Texas, is up against Gina Hinojosa, a state lawmaker who has pulled ahead in the polls in recent weeks. No matter the outcome, it will be record-setting: A win for Mr. Abbott would mean a fourth term as governor, a first in Texas history; a win for Ms. Hinojosa would mean the state’s first Hispanic governor.

Joe Lombardo, a relatively moderate Republican, is looking to win re-election in one of the nation’s most competitive races for governor. He faces the state’s attorney general, Democrat Aaron Ford, who has sought to tie Mr. Lombardo to President Trump. Mr. Ford would be Nevada’s first Black governor.

In an expensive and markedly bitter race, Vivek Ramaswamy, who made millions in pharmaceutical start-ups and briefly ran for president in 2024, is running against Dr. Amy Acton, who was the state’s chief public health officer in the early days of the Covid pandemic.

Representative Tom Tiffany, a Republican with close ties to President Trump, is facing David Crowley, a Democrat and the Milwaukee County executive. Mr. Crowley is hoping to keep the seat in Democratic hands and help his party win a trifecta in Wisconsin.

Gov. Jim Pillen, a Republican, is facing a surprisingly competitive re-election race in a state that has not elected a Democrat as governor in more than 30 years but where many voters are frustrated with federal agricultural policies. His opponent, former State Senator Lynne Walz, has pitched herself to voters as a different kind of Democrat, often noting her Christian faith and her childhood on a hog farm.

Rick Jackson, a health care executive, is aiming to hold the governorship for Republicans in politically mixed Georgia. He is facing Keisha Lance Bottoms, a Democrat and a former mayor of Atlanta. The Republican incumbent, Gov. Brian Kemp, was barred by term limits from running again.

Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson is trying to keep the governor’s office in Democratic hands for a third straight term. She faces Representative John James, a Republican from suburban Detroit, in a state where voters swing regularly between parties.

In a state that has been controlled by Republicans for close to a decade, a surprisingly competitive race for governor has unfolded between Rob Sand, the Democratic state auditor, and Zach Lahn, a Republican supported by the MAHA movement.

Senator Amy Klobuchar, a Democrat, entered the governor’s race early this year after Gov. Tim Walz suspended his campaign for a third term amid a scandal over social services fraud. She is favored to defeat Lisa Demuth, the Republican speaker of the Minnesota House.

Gov. Katie Hobbs of Arizona, the Democratic incumbent, is fighting to keep control of the desert battleground’s highest office. Ms. Hobbs, a moderate, is facing Representative Andy Biggs, a Trump-endorsed former chair of the far-right House Freedom Caucus who’s backed by Turning Point USA.

Deb Haaland, the former Democratic congresswoman and interior secretary, is looking to become the nation’s first female Native American governor. A Republican former mayor, Gregg Hull, is mounting a long-shot challenge notable for the unusual promise he made at its outset: No negative campaigning.

Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders, a Republican, is heavily favored to win a second term. Ms. Sanders, who served as President Trump’s press secretary during his first term, is facing Fred Love, a Democratic state senator.

Gov. Ned Lamont, a Democrat, is seeking a third consecutive term, a feat accomplished only once before in the state. His Republican challenger, Ryan Fazio, a state senator from Greenwich, is grappling with fierce political headwinds. No one in his party has won a statewide election in 20 years.

Hannah Pingree, a Democrat and former Maine House speaker, has maintained a steady lead in polls over Bobby Charles, a conservative Republican. The winner will succeed Gov. Janet Mills, a term-limited Democrat whose conflict with President Trump raised her national profile.

After winning by a closer-than-expected margin four years ago, Gov. Kathy Hochul is hoping that anger with President Trump will turn out Democratic voters and help her comfortably secure a second term over her Republican opponent, Bruce Blakeman, the Nassau County executive.

Josh Shapiro, a Democrat and a potential 2028 presidential contender, is running for re-election against Stacy Garrity, the state treasurer and a retired colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve. With healthy approval numbers statewide, Mr. Shapiro has kept a formidable lead in the polls.

Gov. JB Pritzker, a billionaire Democrat who is believed to be weighing a run for president, is seeking a third term in his solidly Democratic state. Mr. Pritzker, a vocal critic of President Trump, is facing a rematch of his 2022 race with Darren Bailey, a Republican former state senator.
Gov. Brad Little, a Republican, is seeking a third term in a reliably conservative state. Terri Pickens, a lawyer, is the Democratic nominee.

Gov. Larry Rhoden, a Republican, emerged from a competitive primary as a strong favorite to be elected to a full term. Mr. Rhoden, who had been lieutenant governor, ascended to the state’s highest office last year when former Gov. Kristi Noem joined President Trump’s cabinet. He is facing Dan Ahlers, a Democrat who previously served in the State Legislature.

Colorado, a onetime swing state that has veered to the left, is expected to elect Phil Weiser, the state’s Democratic attorney general, as its next governor. Republicans were deeply divided over their own candidate, Victor Marx, a ministry leader and political neophyte.
Xavier Becerra, a Democrat who served as secretary of health and human services in the Biden administration, is favored to defeat Steve Hilton, a former Fox News host endorsed by President Trump.

Gov. Maura Healey, a Democrat and a vocal critic of President Trump, is seeking a second term in her solidly Democratic state. Mike Minogue, a former medical technology executive with conservative views, is the Republican nominee.

Gov. Wes Moore, a Democrat and possible future presidential candidate, is a heavy favorite in his bid for a second term. He is facing a rematch with Dan Cox, a Republican former state legislator who lost to Mr. Moore by a large margin four years ago.

Helena Foulkes, a Democrat who is a former CVS executive, defeated Gov. Dan McKee in her party’s primary to establish herself as a strong favorite in the general election. Her opponents include Aaron Guckian, a Republican, and Ken Block, a businessman running as an independent.

Gov. Josh Green of Hawaii, a Democrat who led his state during the Maui wildfires in 2023, is heavily favored to win a second term in a place where Republicans are rarely competitive in statewide races. Gary Cordery, a businessman, is the Republican nominee.

State Senator Eric Barlow, a Republican who defeated a candidate endorsed by President Trump in the primary election, is widely expected to hold the governorship for his party. Ken Casner, the Democratic nominee, is a military veteran who runs a retail shop and cafe.

house_races.long_description: The retirement of a conservative Democrat in this large, rural congressional district has given Republicans one of their best pickup opportunities of the cycle. Former Gov. Paul LePage, a Tea Party stalwart who is seen as a prime G.O.P recruit, is facing Matt Dunlap, the progressive state auditor.

Representative Jeff Hurd, who lost President Trump’s endorsement after opposing his tariffs but regained it after a lobbying campaign by party leaders, is running for re-election. Recent polling suggests he’s in a tight race against his Democratic challenger, Dwayne Romero, an Army veteran and a former Aspen city councilman.

Representative María Elvira Salazar, a three-term Republican, faces a challenge from Eliott Rodriguez, a first-time candidate and Democrat, in a Miami-based district that leans Republican but has been rocked by the Trump administration’s mass deportations.

Nancy Lacore, a Democratic former Navy admiral who was fired by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, is running against Jenny Costa Honeycutt, a Republican Trump ally. They are facing off in a historically conservative district that was recently gerrymandered to favor Republicans. Still, Democrats believe Ms. Lacore has a chance to flip the seat.

Representative John McGuire, a first-term Republican, faces former Representative Tom Perriello, a Democrat who held a similar seat during the Obama administration, in a race that could signal Democrats’ strength this year. President Trump carried the district, which stretches from Charlottesville to the border with North Carolina, by 12 points in 2024.

Representative Lauren Boebert, an ally of President Trump’s who in 2024 hopscotched into this district from another, handily won her previous election and is favored to win again. She faces Eileen Laubacher, a Democratic Navy veteran, and Douglas Mangeris, a libertarian construction superintendent.

Few expected the race to replace Representative Elise Stefanik, who is not seeking re-election, to be close. But her upstate district, which stretches from the suburbs of Albany to the Canadian border, has been hit hard by President Trump’s tariffs, giving Democrats hope that Blake Gendebien, a dairy farmer, can beat Anthony Constantino, a Trump-backed Republican businessman.

Representative Nick LaLota, a Republican, is running for a third term in a reliably red district extending to the eastern tip of Long Island. The race drew national attention in September when his opponent, Chris Gallant, admitted to posing in an explicit ad campaign modeling bondage gear almost two decades ago.
Shannon Taylor, a prosecutor pitching herself as a law-and-order Democrat, is challenging Representative Rob Wittman, a 10-term Republican, in one of the nation’s most competitive House races.

Representative Tom Barrett, a Republican retired Army officer, is fighting to hold on to his seat in a swing district that Democrats have targeted for a pickup. He faces Will Lawrence, a progressive activist who beat out two more moderate Democrats for the party’s nomination.

Representative Jeff Van Drew joined the Republican Party after voting against President Trump’s impeachment in 2019. He won by 17 points in 2024. Zack Mullock, the mayor of Cape May, N.J., is hoping to flip the seat as a Democrat — just as Mr. Van Drew did in the 2018 midterms.

Representative Don Davis, a centrist Democrat, faces a challenge from Laurie Buckhout, a Republican and a retired Army colonel who narrowly lost to him in 2024. The district has elected Black Democrats since 1992, but North Carolina Republicans have since redrawn it to favor their party.

Representative Mike Lawler, a Republican, has defied political odds by holding on to a suburban New York district that Kamala Harris won in 2024. This year he is facing a challenge from Cait Conley, a Democrat and a military veteran who has sought to tie Mr. Lawler to President Trump.

Sam Forstag, a Democrat backed by progressives like Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, is bidding to replace the retiring Republican incumbent and flip a seat long held by conservatives. Mr. Forstag’s candidacy against Aaron Flint, a Trump-endorsed Republican, is a test for a theory that left-leaning politicians running in G.O.P. strongholds can do better in general elections than moderates.

Representative Jeff Crank, a freshman Republican, is running for re-election in a district that has shifted left in recent years amid population growth in Colorado Springs. Strong fund-raising by his Democratic challenger, Jessica Killin, an Army veteran, has further narrowed the race, which both parties now view as competitive.

Representative Mark Amodei is retiring, and a Democrat has never represented his conservative northern Nevada district. But David Flippo, an Air Force veteran who emerged from the Republican primary with President Trump’s backing, has been weighed down by scandal, giving Teresa Benitez-Thompson, a Democratic former state legislator, hopes of pulling off an upset.

Representative John James, a Republican, is running for governor, leaving open his highly competitive seat in suburban Detroit. Democrats have nominated Christina Hines, a prosecutor, to take on Michael Bouchard, a Republican Army veteran.

Jay Feely, a Republican and former N.F.L. kicker, is trying to defend a Republican-held district in Arizona that includes Scottsdale and a chunk of Phoenix. He faces Dr. Amish Shah, a moderate Democrat and former sideline doctor for the New York Jets.

Representative Juan Ciscomani, a two-term G.O.P. incumbent, is fighting to hold this southeastern district anchored in the suburbs of Tucson. Mr. Ciscomani is facing a challenge from JoAnna Mendoza, who has emphasized her background as a former Marine and her experience growing up in poverty.

Two Republican incumbents, Representatives Young Kim and Ken Calvert, face off in a bid for their political survival after being drawn into the same district by California’s redistricting plan, which favored Democrats. The district, which includes parts of Riverside and Orange counties, is one of the few remaining favorable districts for Republicans in California.

Representative Nick Begich, a Republican in his first term, faces a challenge from Bill Hill, a fisherman and former school administrator who is mounting a competitive campaign as an independent candidate. They will appear alongside two other candidates on Alaska’s top-four ranked-choice ballot.

Two years after Representative Tom Suozzi, a Democrat, narrowly defeated the Republican Mike LiPetri in New York’s Third Congressional District, which includes a section of Long Island and a sliver of Queens, the two are facing a rematch. Mr. Suozzi first won the seat in 2016, vacated it in 2022 to run for governor and reclaimed it in 2024.
house_races.seat_description: Parts of Nassau County and Queens

house_races.long_description: Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, a moderate Democrat who has regularly broken with her party to work across the aisle, won her southwestern Washington seat twice against a hard-line Republican. Now, she’s fighting for a third term against John Braun, a Republican state legislative leader endorsed by President Trump.

Connie Chan, a San Francisco supervisor, received a pivotal endorsement in the race to succeed Representative Nancy Pelosi, whose seat is open for the first time since 1987: Ms. Pelosi herself. Ms. Chan and her opponent, State Senator Scott Wiener, are liberal Democrats who share a desire to expand rights for immigrants and gay and transgender people but differ on housing and public transit policy.

After narrowly flipping a Republican-held seat two years ago, Representative Laura Gillen is running to retain her post in New York’s Fourth Congressional District, which includes portions of Nassau County on Long Island. Ms. Gillen is being challenged by Jeanine Driscoll, a Republican and the receiver of taxes in the town of Hempstead.

The seat of Representative Dave Min, an Orange County Democrat, is more solidly Democratic than it was in the last election cycle, before it was redrawn. He faces Jenny Rae Le Roux, a Republican businesswoman.

Two Democrats are going head to head in this Sacramento district after no Republicans advanced in an open primary. Representative Doris Matsui, 82, faces a generational challenge from Mai Vang, a City Council member who is more than 40 years her junior.

house_races.seat_description: East Houston and rural East Texas

house_races.long_description: Representative Adam Gray, a moderate Democrat who won the seat by fewer than 200 votes two years ago, is facing Kevin Lincoln, a Republican former mayor of Stockton, Calif., who after running unsuccessfully in 2024 is trying again, in a different district.

Representative David Valadao, a Republican, has survived several efforts to oust him from his seat in California’s Central Valley. Democrats hope that Randy Villegas, a progressive political scientist and school board trustee, can succeed on a map that was redrawn to make Mr. Valadao more vulnerable.

Casey Askar, a Republican businessman and former Marine, and Pia Dandiya, a Democrat and former high school principal, are vying to represent a district redrawn by Republican state lawmakers. The new district stretches west from Broward County across the Florida peninsula to Marco Island, on the state’s Gulf Coast.

Representative Bryan Steil, a Republican, is trying to fend off a challenge from Mitchell Berman, a Democrat who is a nurse. Republicans have held the southeastern Wisconsin district for three decades, but Democrats have gained ground there in recent years.

Representative Jared Moskowitz, a two-term Democrat, is fighting to keep his seat after state Republicans redrew the congressional map to favor themselves. Scott Singer, a Republican former mayor, and Peter Jassenoff, the Libertarian candidate, are hoping to win in a district where voters favored Trump in 2024 but rejected him in 2020.

Representative Kathy Castor, a 10-term Democrat who has never faced a close race, is running for re-election in a district in the Tampa area that was redrawn to favor Republicans. She faces Mike Beltran, a Republican former state representative, in a district that Mr. Trump won by about 11 points.

Representative Marcy Kaptur, the longest-serving woman in Congress, is in a rematch against Derek Merrin, a former G.O.P. state lawmaker who challenged her two years ago and lost. This time, Mr. Merrin faces Ms. Kaptur in a newly drawn district that gives Republicans an edge.

Representative Brian Fitzpatrick has been a Republican survivor in a suburban Philadelphia district where President Trump is unpopular. Now Mr. Fitzpatrick faces one of his toughest tests in years against Bob Harvie, a Bucks County commissioner who has tried to make the race about stopping Republican control of Congress.

Representative Derrick Van Orden, a hard-line Republican who attended the Jan. 6, 2021, rally at the Capitol, is facing Rebecca Cooke, a Democrat whom he defeated in 2024. The rural western Wisconsin district went for President Trump the last three elections, but Democrats consider this a prime opportunity to flip it.

Representative Zach Nunn, a two-term Republican and a Trump ally, faces Sarah Trone Garriott, a Democratic state senator and a Lutheran minister, in a closely watched Des Moines-area district. Democrats see an opportunity to flip the seat amid growing economic discontent and frustration with the war in Iran.

house_races.seat_description: Fort Worth suburbs and North Texas

house_races.long_description: Representative Shomari Figures, a Black Democrat, is trying to hold on to his seat in Alabama, which was redrawn after the Supreme Court decision that weakened provisions of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 to favor Republicans like his opponent, Rhett Marques. Republicans hope that this new district, with more white, conservative, rural voters, will be easier to flip.

A Republican firearms influencer, Brandon Herrera, is in a tight race with Katy Padilla Stout, a lawyer and former teacher who has highlighted Mr. Herrera’s absolutist views on gun regulations and his inflammatory online rhetoric. Mr. Herrera has cast her as too liberal for a West Texas border district that President Trump won by 15 points in 2024.

Representative Jen Kiggans, a Republican, is in a rematch against Elaine Luria, the former Democratic representative she unseated four years ago. The two Navy veterans are vying to represent Virginia’s tidewater district, which is deeply intertwined with the U.S. military and affected by the Iran War.

Representative Rob Bresnahan, a first-term Republican representing one of the country’s most competitive districts, is being challenged by Paige Cognetti, the mayor of Scranton. She has accused Mr. Bresnahan, who campaigned on banning stock-trading by members of Congress but became one of the most active traders on Capitol Hill, of profiting from his position.

Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks, a Republican who won re-election by just 799 votes in 2024, faces Christina Bohannan, a Democrat, for a third consecutive election. Major Republican super PACs withdrew millions in planned spending from the southeastern Iowa district, signaling growing doubts about the incumbent’s prospects.

Democrats invested heavily in the campaign of Zach Dembo, viewing his background as a Navy veteran, a former federal prosecutor and a former official under Gov. Andy Beshear as helpful for winning over swing voters. He is running in this conservative district against Dr. Ralph Alvarado, a Trump-backed physician and a former state senator.

Representative Scott Perry, considered one of the most vulnerable House Republicans, two years ago narrowly defeated Janelle Stelson, a former news anchor. Now Ms. Stelson, a Democrat who has run ads embracing parts of Trump’s agenda, is waging a second campaign against Mr. Perry.

Carlos De La Cruz, an Air Force veteran, is trying to deliver an open seat anchored in San Antonio to Republicans, who redrew the district last year to lean red. His opponent, Johnny Garcia, is a former deputy sheriff running as a conservative Democrat.

Representative Ryan Mackenzie, a first-term Republican, is facing Bob Brooks, a Democratic firefighter and union leader, in a competitive Lehigh Valley district. Mr. Mackenzie narrowly flipped the district two years ago but now faces scrutiny from voters over soaring costs and the war with Iran.

Representative Kristen McDonald Rivet, a Democrat, is running for a second term in a district that voted for President Trump in 2024. Her Republican opponent, Tom Smith, won his nomination in unusual fashion: He had initially suspended his campaign, but still managed to beat Trump’s favored candidate, Amir Hassan.

Republican Representative Gabe Evans is trying for a second term against progressive Democrat Manny Rutinel, in a House district north of Denver that mixes working-class communities with ranches and farms. Mr. Evans is a top target of House Democrats, and a win by him would be a significant setback for the party.

Representative Kevin Kiley, a former Republican who this year became an independent, is facing Richard Pan, a former Democratic state senator, in California’s newly redrawn Sixth Congressional District. The district is widely considered favorable to Democrats and includes the city of Sacramento.

The G.O.P. has all but ceded the seat held by Representative Don Bacon, a moderate Republican who is retiring, by withdrawing cash from his district. Denise Powell, a Democratic political organizer, is favored to defeat Brinker Harding, a Republican Omaha city councilman.

Representative Thomas Kean Jr., a Republican, is defending his seat against a strong challenge from Rebecca Bennett, a former Navy pilot who won the Democratic nomination in a romp. Mr. Kean’s campaign lost ground this spring when he was hospitalized for depression, leading him to miss months on Capitol Hill.

Representative Chuck Edwards, a Republican, dropped his re-election bid after the House Ethics Committee released a damning report about his inappropriate conduct toward young female staff members. Republicans have struggled to unify around their replacement candidate, Jennifer Balkcom, a state lawmaker. Her Democratic opponent, Jamie Ager, a farmer, has been leading in recent polling.

Representative Vicente Gonzalez, a Democrat, is defending his seat in a South Texas district that was redrawn to be more favorable to Republicans. His opponent, Eric Flores, is a Trump-endorsed former federal prosecutor and Army veteran.

Representative Derek Tran, an Army veteran and Democrat, is well-positioned to win re-election in his Orange County district, which was redrawn last year. He has also far outraised his Republican opponent, the former mayor of Cerritos, Chuong Vo.

Representative Eugene Vindman, a freshman Democrat, is vying to keep his seat. While Virginia’s top court struck down a new congressional map that would have rendered his district more safely blue, the national political environment this year is favorable for Democrats. Mr. Vindman faces Doug Ollivant, a Republican Army veteran.

house_races.seat_description: North Las Vegas and central counties
Santa Fe with north and east counties

house_races.long_description: The redrawing of California’s congressional map strengthened the position of Representative George Whitesides, a Democrat in northern Los Angeles County. Kamala Harris carried the district by four percentage points in 2024, but would have won by 10 using the new map. Mr. Whitesides faces Jason Gibbs, a Republican city councilman from Santa Clarita.

Representative Byron Donalds is giving up his red seat in Southwest Florida to run for governor. The favorite to fill it is Jim Schwartzel, a radio station owner who prevailed in the Republican primary over a Trump-backed candidate and two scandal-plagued former congressmen. He faces Victor Arias, a Democratic lawyer.

Bobby Pulido, an award-winning Tejano singer, is challenging Representative Monica De La Cruz, a third-term Republican. Running as a conservative Democrat, Mr. Pulido has emphasized that he supports gun rights and border security while embracing Democratic calls for social welfare programs. Polls indicate a competitive race in a district that President Trump won by 18 points in 2024.

house_races.seat_description: Northern border; most of Bergen County
State College and rural north central

house_races.long_description: This district is currently held by a Republican, but the new version, redrawn last year to shift its boundaries from Riverside County west into Los Angeles County, leans heavily Democratic. Representative Linda Sánchez, a Democrat who represents half of the new district, is running for re-election against the Republican Mitch Clemmons, a plumber.

house_races.seat_description: Texas Panhandle to Denton County suburbs

house_races.long_description: Representative Henry Cuellar, an 11-term Democrat, is defending a South Texas district where voters favored President Trump by 10 percentage points in 2024. He is facing Tano Tijerina, the Webb County judge, who changed his party affiliation to Republican from Democrat after Mr. Trump was re-elected in 2024.
house_races.seat_description: Laredo and the Rio Grande Valley
Parts of Columbia and southwest counties

house_races.long_description: Eight years after Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a democratic socialist, surged to prominence by defeating a party stalwart in Queens, she will face off against a little-known and underfunded Republican real estate developer, Diamant Hysenaj. Ms. Ocasio-Cortez appears unconcerned by the challenge and has spent much of this election season campaigning for other Democrats.

house_races.seat_description: North Brooklyn and parts of Queens

measures_races.seat: 2 - Repeal ranked choice voting
measures_races.long_description: Replaces the state’s existing ranked-choice general election system with single-choice elections, replaces open primary elections with partisan primaries and repeals campaign finance rules put in place by a 2020 ballot measure.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Require citizenship to vote
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Ballot Measure 3: Require Citizenship to Vote
measures_races.long_description: Amends the law to specify that only United States citizens have the right to vote in Alaska.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Require elections for lieutenant governor vacancies
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 1: Lieutenant Governor Vacancy Elections
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require an election to fill the office of lieutenant governor if the seat becomes vacant more than 60 days before the next general election. It also allows the State Legislature to set the salaries of the lieutenant governor and officers of the Legislature.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Establish process for school district consolidation
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to establish a process for allowing two or more county school boards to merge their school systems into one multi-county school system.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Allow student-led prayer and require the Pledge of Allegiance
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 3: Pledge of Allegiance and School Prayer
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require public schools to conduct the Pledge of Allegiance daily and to allow for student-led prayer in schools.

measures_races.seat: 4 - Require The Star-Spangled Banner in public schools
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 4: Star-Spangled Banner in Public Schools
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require public schools to broadcast or arrange a performance of the first stanza of the national anthem at least once per week.

measures_races.seat: 141 - Prohibit vehicle miles traveled tax
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition 141: Prohibit Tax on Vehicle Miles Traveled
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit taxes based on the number of miles traveled in a motor vehicle. It would also prohibit the State Legislature from making laws limiting miles traveled in a motor vehicle.

measures_races.seat: 142 - Prohibit race-based preferential treatment or discrimination
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit state agencies, including public schools, from requiring preferential treatment toward or discrimination against someone on the basis of race, ethnicity or other classes. It also prohibits requiring that applicants, employees or students provide a statement in support of race-based diversity, equity and inclusion.

measures_races.seat: 144 - Require voter ID and citizenship to vote
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require government-issued identification and proof of U.S. citizenship to vote in local elections, including when voting by mail, and to prohibit noncitizens from making campaign contributions.

measures_races.seat: 316 - Limit local grocery taxes
measures_races.long_description: Prohibits local governments from enacting a grocery tax without voter approval through June 2027 and caps any new or increased grocery tax after that at 2 percent.

measures_races.seat: 317 - Drug cartel terrorist designation
measures_races.long_description: Declares drug cartels to be terrorist organizations and directs the state’s Department of Homeland Security to do everything in its authority to address any threats posed by them.

measures_races.seat: 318 - Require school facility access based on sex assigned at birth
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition 318: Restrictions on Trans Athletes and Bathroom Access
measures_races.long_description: Requires all schools and athletic associations to designate athletic teams as male, female or co-ed based on the sex of the athletes as recorded at birth. Bars students, athletes, employees and others from joining sports teams or from using school and athletic association facilities, including restrooms, that are not designated for their sex assigned at birth.

measures_races.seat: 319 - Prohibit traffic photo enforcement systems without voter approval
measures_races.long_description: Prohibits government agencies from installing new photo enforcement systems for traffic ticketing, and requires voter approval at the next general election and every 10 years after to continue using systems signed into contract before the end of 2026.

measures_races.seat: 320 - School district spending requirements
measures_races.long_description: Requires large school districts to spend at least 60 percent of their budget on “direct instructional expenses,” which would be determined by the auditor general.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Authorize veteran and housing bonds
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes the state to issue $11.25 billion in bonds to fund housing affordability programs, including $1.25 billion for the state’s veteran home loan program.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Modify budget stabilization fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to raise the limit on the state’s budget reserve fund to 20 percent of its general fund revenue from the current 10 percent ceiling.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Permanently extend high-income tax for school funding
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to make permanent certain tax rates on high incomes that were approved by voters in 2012 and are set to expire in 2031, allocating the revenue to public schools and community colleges.

measures_races.seat: 37 - Create middle-income homebuyer loan program
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $25 billion in bonds to establish a loan program offering fixed-rate mortgages to middle-income homebuyers who provide a down payment of at least 3 percent on qualifying new homes.

measures_races.seat: 38 - Authorize immunotherapy research bonds
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $8.4 billion in bonds to fund immunology and immunotherapy research.

measures_races.seat: 39 - Require voter ID
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require citizens to present government-issued identification to vote in person or to provide a government-issued identification number to vote by mail.

measures_races.seat: 4 - Repeal ban on public campaign finance
measures_races.long_description: Repeals a ban on public financing of election campaigns and allows the state and local governments to create programs to support candidates using public funds.

measures_races.seat: 40 - Impose one-time wealth tax over $1 billion
measures_races.long_description: Imposes a one-time 5 percent tax on individuals and trusts with over $1 billion in assets, and allocates the resulting revenues to fund health care, food assistance and education.

measures_races.seat: 41 - Require audit of programs funded by special taxes
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit any new state taxes whose revenues are excluded from the state spending limit, and to require audits of certain programs funded by special taxes.

measures_races.seat: 42 - Prohibit new state taxes on personal property
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition 42: Prohibit New Personal Property Taxes
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit new state taxes on personal property, including financial assets, business holdings and intellectual property.

measures_races.seat: 43 - Raise approval threshold for voter-initiated special taxes
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require two-thirds voter approval to impose, extend or increase voter-proposed local special taxes.

measures_races.seat: 44 - Health clinic revenue spending requirements
measures_races.long_description: Requires certain nonprofit community health clinics to spend at least 90 percent of their revenue on patient care and services, rather than on management and overhead.

measures_races.seat: 45 - Modify environmental review to expedite projects
measures_races.long_description: Expedites environmental reviews for certain types of projects, including most housing, transportation, water and health projects.

measures_races.seat: 5 - Require separate election for recalled officials
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require separate elections to recall state officials and to fill their vacated seats.

measures_races.seat: 132 - Increase penalties for fentanyl crimes
measures_races.long_description: Increases the felony classifications and penalties for the manufacturing, distribution, sale and possession of fentanyl.

measures_races.seat: 133 - Life imprisonment for trafficking minors
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition 133: Life Imprisonment for Human Trafficking of Minors
measures_races.long_description: Requires that anyone convicted of trafficking a minor be sentenced to life in prison without parole or release.

measures_races.seat: 134 - Require school sports participation based on biological sex
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition 134: Trans Athletes’ Participation in School Sports
measures_races.long_description: Requires student athletes to participate on teams that match their sex assigned at birth, and requires schools, colleges and athletic associations to designate sports teams as male, female or coeducational.

measures_races.seat: 135 - Prohibit gender-affirming surgery for minors
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition 135: Prohibit Gender Confirmation Surgery for Minors
measures_races.long_description: Prohibits health care professionals from providing surgeries to people under 18 for the purpose of altering their sex characteristics.

measures_races.seat: 136 - Cap individual and corporate income tax at 4.4%
measures_races.long_description: Establishes a 4.4 percent cap on individual and corporate income tax rates.

measures_races.seat: 137 - Use sporting goods sales tax revenue for environmental conservation
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition 137: Sporting Goods Sales Tax Revenue for Conservation
measures_races.long_description: Allows the state to spend a portion of revenue from the sales tax on sporting goods on environmental conservation.

measures_races.seat: 81 - Require law enforcement to coordinate with DHS regarding immigration status
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 81: Require Law Enforcement to Coordinate With D.H.S. on Immigration
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require law enforcement to notify the Department of Homeland Security when charging someone with a violent crime (or any crime, if the person has a prior felony conviction) if that person’s immigration status cannot be determined.

measures_races.seat: 82 - Establish right to purchase and sell natural gas
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 82: Purchase and Sale of Natural Gas
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to grant the right to purchase and sell natural gas for cooking or heating in homes and businesses.

measures_races.seat: 83 - Establish constitutional right to hunt and fish
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 83: Right to Hunt and Fish
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to grant the right to hunt and fish.

measures_races.seat: 84 - Require voter signature and identification number on the outside of mail ballots
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 84: Voter Signature and ID Requirement
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require voters casting ballots by mail to provide both their signature and an identification number.

measures_races.seat: 85 - Require ballot questions to be written in plain language
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 85: Plain Language Ballot Questions
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require ballot questions to be written in plain language at no more than an eighth-grade reading level.

measures_races.seat: 86 - Clarify congressional redistricting process
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require any mid-decade redistricting plan to be approved by the congressional redistricting commission and the State Supreme Court, and prohibits the approval of any map that has been drawn to purposely favor one political party.

measures_races.seat: 87 - Replace the uniform income tax rate with a graduated tax structure
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to replace the uniform tax rate requirement with a graduated income tax, and authorizes the state to use the additional revenue generated by the change to supplement current funding for K-12 public school education, health care and early child care programs.

measures_races.seat: NN - Increase TABOR revenue cap for K-12 funding
measures_races.long_description: Increases spending on public schools by 2 percent each year for the next 10 years by raising the annual limit on state fiscal year spending.

measures_races.seat: 86 - Prohibit the force-feeding of birds
measures_races.long_description: Prohibits the force-feeding of birds and the sale, distribution or import of any products of fattened bird livers, such as foie gras.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Modify budget stabilization fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to increase the amount of funds that can be retained in the budget stabilization fund to 25 percent from 10 percent of net general revenue.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Exempt tangible personal property on agricultural land from taxation
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 2: Personal Property on Agricultural Land Tax Exemption
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to exempt physical personal property on agricultural land from property taxes if it is used for farming or agritourism.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Create new homestead tax exemption
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to increase the homestead tax exemption and decrease the cap on how much the assessed value of non-homestead properties can increase each year to 5 percent from 10 percent.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Increase acreage limit for conservation tax program
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 1: Increase Acreage for Conservation Tax Program
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to increase the amount of property a single owner can register under Georgia’s conservation use classification, which means the land is taxed at a lower rate, to 4,000 acres from 2,000.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Nonpartisan probate judge elections
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 2: Nonpartisan Probate Judge Elections
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require that all probate judges be elected in nonpartisan elections.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Create next generation 911 fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to allow the government to create a dedicated fund to expand, maintain and operate emergency communications systems.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Extend timeline for judicial confirmations
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to increase the amount of time the Senate has to consider and act on judicial appointments made between April 1 and Dec. 31.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Issue Resilient Infrastructure for Shelter and Equity bonds
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to allow the Legislature to empower counties and municipalities to issue housing infrastructure growth bonds for public works and improvements.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 1 - Require annual funding for a Food Security Fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to create a food security fund and increase total annual funding for this and other special funds to 3 percent of estimated real property tax revenues.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 10 - Require the City to prepare and maintain a ten-year affordable housing plan
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to require the director of housing and land management to create and maintain a 10-year plan for the development of affordable housing and to provide updates every five years.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 11 - Allow certain funds to award grants to tax-exempt non-profits
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to allow the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund and the Climate Resiliency Fund to award grants to tax-exempt nonprofits that provide services relevant to each fund’s scope.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 12 - Allow special funds to receive funding from sources other than real property tax revenue
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 12: Funding Sources for Special Funds
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to allow certain special funds to receive funding from federal, state, philanthropic and other sources.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 13 - Allow the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund to be used for historic preservation
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 13: Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to rename the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund as the Land, Natural Resources and Historic Preservation Fund, and expands its scope to include historic preservation projects.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 14 - Increase funding for management of lands acquired through the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 14: Increased Appropriation for Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to increase the annual appropriation for costs related to operating, maintaining and managing the lands acquired using the Clean Water and Natural Lands Fund to 10 percent of the money deposited into the fund from 5 percent.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 15 - Establish Office of Data and Innovation
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 15: Office of Data and Innovation
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to establish the Office of Data and Innovation to improve city services, promote government transparency and ensure that the city uses artificial intelligence responsibly.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 16 - Allow permanent resident aliens to serve on City boards and commissions
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 16: City Board and Commissions Eligibility
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to allow non-citizen permanent residents of Honolulu to serve on city boards and commissions.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 17 - Exclude vacancies and non-voting members from quorum and allow approval by a majority of present members
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 17: Excluding Vacancies From Quorum Votes
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to stipulate that the presence of a majority of the members of a board or commission, excluding vacancies and non-voting members, shall constitute a quorum.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 18 - Exempt the First Deputy of the Department of Human Resources from civil service
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 18: First Deputy of the Department of Human Resources Exemption
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to exempt the first deputy of the Department of Human Resources from civil service provisions.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 19 - Require the City Clerk to provide technical and secretarial services to the Charter Commission
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to require the city clerk to provide technical and administrative support to the Charter Commission.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 2 - Add language to Charter’s preamble recognizing ʻāina, kūpuna, and Prince Kūhiō
measures_races.long_description: Amends the preamble of the Honolulu Charter to include language recognizing Native Hawaiian cultural values and the relationship between the people of Honolulu and the ʻāina, or land.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 20 - Remove eligibility of impeached city officials to be elected or appointed to any City office for two years
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to prohibit impeached council members, mayors or prosecuting attorneys from holding public office for two years after impeachment.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 3 - Establish Office of ʻŌiwi Resources and Cultural Stewardship
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 3: Office of ʻŌiwi Resources and Cultural Stewardship
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to establish the Office of ʻŌiwi Resources and Cultural Stewardship to promote and protect Native Hawaiian culture.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 4 - Establish LGBTQIA+ Commission
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to establish a nine-member L.G.B.T.Q.I.A.+ Commission to advise the mayor, City Council and city agencies.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 5 - Use ranked choice voting to elect the Mayor, City Council, and Prosecuting Attorney
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to adopt ranked-choice voting for mayoral, City Council and prosecuting attorney elections, beginning in 2032.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 6 - Ensure constitutional rights are protected regardless of citizenship or immigration status
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 6: Law Enforcement Compliance With Federal Immigration Enforcement
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to require the Honolulu Police Department to ensure the constitutional rights of all people, regardless of immigration or citizenship status, and to allow the department to work with federal immigration enforcement only when required by statute or court order.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 7 - Add a statement to the Charter encouraging housing availability as a City policy
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to include a statement about the importance of increasing housing availability and preserving available housing.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 8 - Clarify that the Affordable Housing Fund is a revolving fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to clarify that the Affordable Housing Fund is a revolving fund, meaning that repayments, interest, earnings and proceeds are deposited into the fund.

measures_races.seat: Honolulu 9 - Remove requirement for a second public hearing for any transaction related to City real property interests
measures_races.long_description: Amends the Honolulu Charter to eliminate a requirement for a second public hearing for city property transactions.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Require two-thirds legislative vote for income tax increase
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 1: Two-Thirds Vote for Income Tax Increase
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require a two-thirds supermajority vote in both state legislative chambers to increase or pass new income taxes.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Establish right to abortion
measures_races.long_description: Establishes the right to reproductive freedom and privacy, including the right to abortion up to the point of fetal viability.

measures_races.seat: HJR 4 - Prohibit drug legalization through initiatives
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment HJR 4: Prohibit Citizen-Led Drug Legalization
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to remove citizens’ ability to initiate drug-legalization measures, and to state that only the Legislature has the authority to legalize drugs.

measures_races.seat: HJR 6 - Establish English as official state language
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment HJR 6: English as State Language
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to designate English as Idaho’s official language.

measures_races.seat: Chicago-1 - Restart the use of gunshot detection technology
measures_races.long_description: Reinstates the use of technology that alerts first responders when gunshots are detected.

measures_races.seat: Chicago-2 - Develop a permanent festival and outdoor event space
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 2: Festival and Outdoor Event Space
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes the city to develop a permanent festival and outdoor space for large-scale events.

measures_races.seat: Chicago-3 - Seek compensation for the cost of federal immigration operations in Chicago
measures_races.long_description: Allows the city to seek financial compensation from the federal government for the economic harm caused by ICE operations in Chicago.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Require citizenship to vote
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 1: Require Citizenship to Vote
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to specify that one must be a United States citizen in order to be eligible to vote.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Limit governor’s pardon and commutation power
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit the governor from issuing a pardon or commuting a sentence in the period from 60 days before a gubernatorial election to the fifth Tuesday after the election.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Allow one-time transfer of disabled veteran property tax exemption
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 1: Property Tax Exemption for Spouses of Disabled Veterans
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to allow the spouse of a deceased disabled veteran to transfer a special property tax exemption once to a new home.

measures_races.seat: 10 - Authorize a property tax exemption for rehabilitated properties
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 10: Rehabilitated Property Tax Exemption
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to allow a property tax exemption for previously uninhabitable property that has been rehabilitated.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Adjust property tax millage rates
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to allow higher millage rates for property taxes than were set by the previous year’s assessment, up to the maximum approved by voters, without holding a new election.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Prohibit post-conviction bail if convicted of an aggravated offense against a minor
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit post-conviction bail for those convicted of an aggravated offense against a minor.

measures_races.seat: 4 - Change gubernatorial term limit
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to change the gubernatorial term limit from two consecutive terms to a lifetime maximum of two terms.

measures_races.seat: 5 - Remove requirement that retirement systems must pay oldest debts first
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 5: Remove Payment Order Requirement
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to remove a requirement that certain retirement systems pay their oldest debt first.

measures_races.seat: 6 - Authorize additional property tax exemption for senior citizens
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 6: Property Tax Exemption for Seniors
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to allow a property tax exemption of up to $30,000 for seniors who qualify for an income-based assessment freeze.

measures_races.seat: 7 - Allow use of public funds to remove or replace hazardous service lines on private property
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 7: Public Funds for Drinking Water Maintenance
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to allow the use of public funds for the maintenance of drinking water service lines affected by hazardous materials.

measures_races.seat: 8 - Prohibit expropriation of property by a foreign adversary
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 8: Property Expropriation by Foreign Adversaries
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit foreign adversaries from using expropriation laws to force the sale of property.

measures_races.seat: 9 - Increase income limit for senior property tax assessment
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 9: Income Limits for Property Tax Assessment
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to raise the income limit for a special property tax assessment for certain homeowners to $150,000 from $100,000.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Expand Public Records Law to governor and legislative offices
measures_races.long_description: Makes most records held by the governor’s office and the legislature public records, with the exception of documents related to policy development and certain communications between legislators and their constituents.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Allow Committee for Public Counsel Services employees to engage in collective bargaining
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 2: Committee for Public Counsel Services Collective Bargaining
measures_races.long_description: Allows employees of the Committee for Public Counsel Services to form a union and engage in collective bargaining.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Top-two primary elections
measures_races.long_description: Eliminates primary elections based on political party and instead establishes a single primary in which all candidates appear on the same ballot, with the two who receive the most votes advancing to the general election.

measures_races.seat: 4 - Allow Election Day voter registration
measures_races.long_description: Permits people to register to vote on Election Day.

measures_races.seat: 5 - Modify state tax revenue limit methodology
measures_races.long_description: Changes the limit on how much tax revenue the state can collect in a year to the previous year’s revenue, increased by a rate equal to the average wage and salary growth over the previous three years.

measures_races.seat: 6 - Establish Nature for All conservation fund
measures_races.long_description: Creates a fund for environmental conservation that would receive tax revenue collected on the sale and use of sporting goods, recreational vehicles and golf courses.

measures_races.seat: 7 - Reduce minimum lot sizes for single-family homes
measures_races.long_description: Allows single-family homes across the state to be built in residentially zoned areas if the land is at least 5,000 square feet in area, has at least 50 feet of land bordering the street it faces and has access to public sewer and water services.

measures_races.seat: 8 - Repeal recreational marijuana legalization
measures_races.long_description: Repeals the laws that legalize, regulate and tax the sale of recreational marijuana and changes the penalties for possession.

measures_races.seat: 9 - Repeal HB4885 firearm regulations
measures_races.long_description: Upholds a law passed through the legislature that increases the regulation of firearms, including ghost guns, machine guns and assault-style weapons.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Modify state employee collective bargaining rules
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require the state budget to include funding to cover employment agreements between the state and its employees.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Allow temporary appointments to fill Commission on Judicial Disabilities vacancies
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution so that, in the case of a vacancy on the Commission on Judicial Disabilities, the chairperson may fill it with a temporary appointment of a former member or the governor may appoint a substitute or extend the term of an existing member.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Clarify that state redistricting requirements apply only to state legislative districts
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to clarify that existing districting requirements apply only to the state’s legislative districts, not its congressional districts, and authorizes the General Assembly to grant jurisdiction to the State Supreme Court to review challenges to congressional redistricting plans.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Modify Permanent School Fund distribution rules
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Amendment 1: Permanent School Fund Distribution Rules
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to change how the Permanent School Fund is managed and invested, to increase funding for public school districts.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Repeal right to abortion and prohibit gender transition for minors
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 3: Repeal Right to Abortion and Prohibit Gender Transition Care for Minors
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to repeal the right to abortion, except in certain cases, and to prohibit gender transition procedures for minors.

measures_races.seat: 6 - Require 80% voter approval to confirm legislative changes to voter-approved initiatives
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Amendment 6: Raise Threshold for Changing Voter-Approved Initiatives
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit the State Legislature from repealing or amending a voter-approved initiative unless at least 80 percent of both the state House and Senate vote to refer the change to the ballot and voters approve it.

measures_races.seat: 7 - Create Show-Me Prosperity Fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to create a permanent public endowment to support state government, with the goal of its investment earnings being able to eliminate state-imposed taxes.

measures_races.seat: 8 - Require election of county sheriffs
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require the election of county sheriffs every four years, establish sheriffs as the chief law enforcement officers in those counties and limit the removal of sheriffs from office.

measures_races.seat: A - Referendum on the 2025 congressional redistricting map
measures_races.long_description: Upholds the new congressional district map that was signed into law in 2025, which makes most changes to the Kansas City area.

measures_races.seat: 132 - Require judicial elections to remain nonpartisan
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require that state judicial elections remain nonpartisan.

measures_races.seat: 133 - Protect the right to initiative and referendum
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Initiative 133: Protecting the Right to Initiative and Referendum
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to protect the right to referendum without government interference. Requires impartial, predictable, open and timely processes for ballot issues.

measures_races.seat: 194 - Prohibit artificial persons from providing political contributions or support
measures_races.long_description: Prohibits “artificial persons,” including nonprofits, trusts, partnerships, corporations, trade associations or unincorporated associations doing business in the state, from contributing to political campaigns.

measures_races.seat: HB 1089 - Limit local property tax increase
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment HB 1089: Limit Property Tax Increase
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require limits on property tax increases.

measures_races.seat: Raleigh-1 - Housing bonds
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $101.5 million in bonds to fund the construction or rehabilitation of affordable housing and affordable housing programs.

measures_races.seat: Raleigh-2 - Transportation bonds
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $101.5 million in bonds to fund transportation-related improvements.

measures_races.seat: SB 1080 - Lower income tax rate cap
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment SB 1080: Lower Income Tax Rate Cap
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to reduce the maximum income tax rate to 3.5 percent from 7 percent.

measures_races.seat: SB 921 - Require voter ID
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment SB 921: Voter ID Requirement
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require all voters, including those who vote by mail, to present photo identification.

measures_races.seat: 1 - 60% voter approval for amendments
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require that any constitutional amendment receive 60 percent voter approval to pass, rather than the current threshold of a simple majority.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Free school meals
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require that all public schools provide free breakfast and lunch to students.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Increase legislative term limits
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to increase the term limit for state legislators to three consecutive terms from two.

measures_races.seat: 440 - Allow online sports wagering
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to authorize laws governing sports betting in the state.

measures_races.seat: 441 - Regulate online sports wagering
measures_races.long_description: Allows online sports betting in the state and authorizes the gaming commission to regulate it.

measures_races.seat: 442 - Require school sports participation based on biological sex
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Initiative 442: Trans Athletes’ Participation in School Sports
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require schools to designate sports teams as male, female or coeducational, and prohibits male participation on female teams.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Abolish register of probate
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 1: Abolish Register of Probate
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to eliminate the Register of Probate office and any references to it.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Issue senior citizen bonds
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $30 million in bonds to fund improvements to senior citizen facilities.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Require governor action on passed legislation and eliminate pocket veto
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 1: Governor Action on Passed Legislation
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require that bills become law if the governor does not sign or veto them in the required time frame, and to require the governor to submit an explanation for any vetoes.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Allow school elections to coincide with partisan elections
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to remove the requirement that school elections be held separately from partisan elections.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Issue public library bonds
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $20 million in bonds to fund public and school library acquisitions.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Establish nominating committees for Board of Regents appointments
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 3: Board of Regents Nominating Committees
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to establish nominating committees for the state’s Boards of Regents, the governing bodies that manage public universities.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Issue higher education bonds
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $230 million in bonds to fund capital improvements and acquisitions at public colleges, special schools and tribal schools.
