measures_races.seat: 4 - Establish state legislator salaries based on median income
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to set the salary for state legislators as equal to that of the state’s median household income.

measures_races.seat: 6 - Right to abortion
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to include the right to an abortion until the point of fetal viability or in cases in which an abortion would protect the life or health of the pregnant patient.

measures_races.seat: 7 - Require voter ID
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require voters to present photo identification when voting in person or to verify their identity when voting by mail.

measures_races.seat: 845 - Change judicial nominating commission
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to change the Judicial Nominating Commission structure, including requiring that appointments be made according to congressional districts and allowing commissioners to serve two consecutive six-year terms.

measures_races.seat: 847 - Reduce annual property value assessment increases
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 847: Reduce Annual Property Value Assessment Increases
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to reduce the annual growth limit of property valuations used to calculate certain taxes.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Issue higher education bond
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $275 million in bonds to fund the construction and improvement of higher education facilities.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Issue housing and development bond
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $120 million in bonds to fund the increase and preservation of affordable housing.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Issue economic development bond
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $100 million in bonds to fund economic and infrastructure development, including projects supporting the state’s oceans.

measures_races.seat: 4 - Issue cultural and historical project bond
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 4: Cultural and Historical Project Bonds
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $50 million in bonds to fund historical and cultural projects, including the construction of a history center and the funding of grants awarded by the Rhode Island Historical Preservation and Heritage Commission for capital improvements to public historic sites, museums and cultural art centers.

measures_races.seat: 5 - Issue environmental protection bond
measures_races.long_description: Authorizes $55 million in bonds to fund environmental, recreational and water infrastructure projects.

measures_races.seat: I - Medicaid expansion contingent on federal funding
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment I: Medicaid Expansion Limits
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to make the state’s expanded Medicaid coverage contingent on the federal government funding at least 90 percent of the program.

measures_races.seat: J - Require citizenship to vote
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment J: Require Citizenship to Vote
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to specify that one must be a United States citizen in order to vote in elections.

measures_races.seat: K - Establish unclaimed property trust fund
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment K: Unclaimed Property Fund
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to establish a fund for abandoned financial assets.

measures_races.seat: L - Raise approval threshold for ballot amendments
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment L: Approval Threshold for Constitutional Amendments
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to increase the threshold to pass a constitutional amendment to 60 percent voter approval from a simple majority.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Change allowances for denial of bail
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit bail in cases where the presumption of guilt is great and the defendant is accused of certain offenses, including any for which a convicted defendant could not be released before serving 85 percent of the sentence.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Prohibit state property tax
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 2: Prohibit State Property Tax
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit the legislature from imposing a property tax.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Expand rights for crime victims
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to expand the rights of crime victims to include communication with the prosecution and the right to be free from intimidation, harassment and abuse throughout the criminal justice system.

measures_races.seat: Austin A - Issue parks and recreation bond
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition A: Parks and Recreation Bonds
measures_races.long_description: Allocates $260 million in bonds to fund infrastructure projects, including buildings and parks.

measures_races.seat: Austin B - Issue library bond
measures_races.long_description: Allocates $35 million in bonds to fund the renovation, rehabilitation and expansion of two public library branches.

measures_races.seat: Austin C - Clarify independence of the Independent Citizens Redistricting Commission
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition C: Independent Citizens Redistricting Commission Independence
measures_races.long_description: Amends the city charter to clarify that the Independent Citizens Redistricting Commission is independent of City Council control.

measures_races.seat: Austin D - Remove the City Council weekly meeting requirement from the City Charter
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition D: City Council Meeting Requirements
measures_races.long_description: Deletes language from the city charter that stipulates the City Council must meet at least once a week.

measures_races.seat: Austin E - Remove the City Council requirement to determine its rules and order of business by ordinance
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition E: City Council Rules and Order of Business
measures_races.long_description: Deletes language from the city charter that requires the City Council to determine its rules and order of business by ordinance.

measures_races.seat: Austin F - Modify campaign finance limits each year by January 1 instead of with the adoption of the budget
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition F: Annual Campaign Finance Modifications
measures_races.long_description: Amends the City Charter to require that campaign finance limits be modified each year by Jan. 1 instead of when the budget is adopted.

measures_races.seat: Austin G - Clarify timing of initiative and charter amendment elections
measures_races.long_description: Amends the City Charter to stipulate the timing of initiative and charter amendment elections.

measures_races.seat: Austin H - Transfer the appointment authority of the City Attorney from the City Manager to the City Council
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition H: City Attorney Appointment Authority
measures_races.long_description: Amends the City Charter to give the City Council the authority to appoint and remove the city attorney.

measures_races.seat: Austin I - Require an Independent Affordability and Efficiency Initiative
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition I: Independent Affordability and Efficiency Initiative
measures_races.long_description: Amends the City Charter to require an Independent Affordability and Efficiency Initiative on a regular basis.

measures_races.seat: Austin J - Allow non-substantive changes and corrections to City Charter language
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Proposition J: Nonsubstantive City Charter Changes
measures_races.long_description: Amends the City Charter to allow for nonsubstantive changes to the charter such as fixes to typographical errors, punctuation and sentence structure.

measures_races.seat: A - Require publication of amendments 60 days before the election
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment A: Publication of Proposed Amendments
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to require that constitutional amendments be published 60 days before the election in which the amendment is scheduled to be on the ballot.

measures_races.seat: B - Raise approval threshold for new or raised taxes
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment B: Approval Threshold for New Taxes
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to increase the voter approval threshold for certain tax changes to 60 percent from a simple majority.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Establish right to abortion
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to establish a right to reproductive freedom, while allowing the state to regulate abortion during the third trimester, except when the patient’s health is at risk or the pregnancy is not viable.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Remove constitutional same-sex marriage provision
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to remove the ban on same-sex marriage and require that all legally valid marriages be treated equally under the law.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Restore felon voting rights
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 3: Felon Voting Rights Upon Release
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to provide that those convicted of felonies have their voting rights restored upon release from incarceration.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Establish parental rights
measures_races.long_description: Reenacts a previous law that gives parents the right to receive notification about medical services being offered to their child at school and the right to opt their child out of certain classes.

measures_races.seat: 638 - Require school sports participation based on biological sex
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Measure 638: Trans Athletes’ Participation in School Sports
measures_races.long_description: Prohibits students who were assigned male at birth from competing with or against female student athletes in sports for female students only. Requires students who choose to participate in such activities to provide a statement from a health care provider verifying their sex.

measures_races.seat: 645 - Repeal and prohibit income tax
measures_races.long_description: Repeals the income tax on households with an income over $1 million and prohibits the state from enacting new individual income taxes.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Prohibit Governor’s partial veto to create or increase any tax or fee
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 1: Prohibit Governor’s Partial Veto to Impose Tax
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit the governor from using a partial veto to impose or increase a state tax.

measures_races.seat: 2 - Prohibit the closure of places of worship during emergencies
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Question 2: Places of Worship Open During Emergencies
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit the state from closing places of worship during emergencies, including public health emergencies.

measures_races.seat: 3 - Prohibit governmental entities from discriminating or granting preferential treatment
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to prohibit government entities, including public colleges and universities, from discriminating or granting preferential treatment on the basis of race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Require citizenship to vote
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Constitutional Amendment 1: Require Citizenship to Vote
measures_races.long_description: Amends the State Constitution to specify that only United States citizens may vote in elections.

measures_races.seat: 1 - Establish a homeowner property tax exemption for primary residences
measures_races.ballot_measure_text: Initiative 1: Homeowner Property Tax Exemption for Primary Residences
measures_races.long_description: Establishes a property tax exemption for a homeowner’s primary residence equal to 50 percent of the property’s value.

statewide_exec_races.long_description: Kris W. Kobach, a Republican who helped make concerns about illegal voting a national issue, is seeking a second term as state attorney general. Democrats have invested heavily in the campaign of Chris Mann, a former police officer and prosecutor who narrowly lost to Mr. Kobach four years ago.

Keith Ellison, a Democrat seeking a third term as attorney general, is in a tight contest against a first-time Republican candidate, Ron Schutz, a trial lawyer. Mr. Schutz has cast Mr. Ellison as partially responsible for a fraud scandal involving state social services programs.

New York’s attorney general, Letitia James, a Democrat, has made headlines for her legal battles with President Trump. As she seeks a third consecutive term, she faces a challenge from Saritha Komatireddy, a Republican former federal prosecutor who has accused Ms. James of not using the office’s full powers to help New Yorkers.
